answers.rationale: Rollout completed 09:03; cache TTL for cluster.local fell from 30 to 5 s; CoreDNS queries rose about 5.7x by 09:05 and saturated CPU limits; DNS latency then reached both orders-api (via per-call resolution) and payment-worker.
Redis was healthy with normal latency and no errors from 08:53, before symptoms began at 09:04.
CoreDNS query rate stayed flat through the 10 -> 30 pod scale-out on an unchanged node set; the node-local caches, not pod count, determine upstream query rate.
Retries on DNS timeouts occurred in the relevant window, but idempotency-key behaviour and gateway capture records are unavailable; nothing discriminates retry-induced duplicates from other causes.
The rollout is an origin condition: it is not produced by any other in-case condition, and its TTL change increases upstream query rate.
Throttling is itself produced by the query-rate increase and transmits it to orders-api through slow lookups on every pricing call.
The failover preceded the errors, but Redis was healthy and error-free before and throughout.
The extra log lines are pricing-failure warnings (a shared downstream cause); disk stayed below 20% and shipping is asynchronous with drop-on-overflow, so log volume does not drive latency.
The scale-out was triggered by slow requests (reverse direction) and did not change the CoreDNS query rate.
The sidecar's 60 s resolution cache and connection reuse kept inventory call latency unchanged while pricing calls degraded.
The image patch and CPU limit increase were applied together; the improvement cannot be attributed to either change, and nothing shows the patch had no effect.
DNS latency is produced upstream by CoreDNS saturation and transmits it to payment-worker; attempts without DNS timeouts ran normally.
Restores the 30 s cache and removes the origin of the query increase, which persisted at 22-24k/s until 10:30 despite the 09:40 CoreDNS change.
The scale-out is an effect, not a cause; 30 pods are near their 64-request limit (58 average), so 10 pods could not hold the load and rejections would increase.
Log volume has no causal effect on latency; the change offers no evidence-supported benefit.
Targets a condition that preceded but did not cause the errors.
Removes the component that is preventing DNS latency from reaching inventory calls, exposing a second call path to the same failure.
Resolves the evidence gap that leaves H4 unknown.

missingInformation: Separate effects of the CoreDNS image patch and the CPU limit increase.
payment-worker idempotency-key behaviour and gateway capture logs for the duplicate charges.
hardness.reasoningChain: chart 2.4.0 rollout (E02) -> cluster.local cache TTL 30 s to 5 s (E03) -> CoreDNS query rate 5.7x and CPU throttling (E04) -> pod DNS latency and timeouts (E05) -> per-call resolution in orders-api pricing client (E06, E13) -> pricing latency near the 3 s ingress timeout -> 502s (E01); in parallel DNS timeouts -> payment-worker backlog (E14).
constructTraps: Treating the Redis failover as causal because it immediately preceded the errors.
Treating log volume as causal because it co-varies with latency.
Treating the scale-out as a cause of DNS load (reverse direction).
Attributing the 09:40 improvement to one of two confounded changes.
Classifying intermediate links (throttling, DNS latency) as origins.
Missing the preventing role of the inventory sidecar.
